images.caption: Figure 1.OmniLatent generates geometry, deformation, appearance, and coherent surface part IDs from a single image in a unified latent space.

Figure 2.Unified Latent Modeling and Pretraining. OmniLatent performs 3D part decomposition through unified latent modeling. Geometry, deformation, appearance, and binary part IDs are encoded into a shared OmniLatent space, then generated by an MM-DiT backbone from an input image with optional 2D mask conditions. The aligned latent space allows geometric and visual priors to support surface part segmentation, and the pretrained model can further be adapted for point-prompted control and amodal part completion. The left branch shows the cascaded VAE decoder: SDF reconstruction defines the surface, whose vertices subsequently query deformation, appearance, and Part IDs from the same latent tokens.

Figure 3.Unified part segmentation and refinementusing images, 2D masks, and point prompts. We adopt an MM-DiT architecture that integrates multiple control signals: interactive regions and geometric conditions are injected via channel concatenation with the noisy latent, while other conditions are incorporated through sequence concatenation.

Figure 4.Amodal part completion.Given full geometry and partial surface masks for all parts, OmniLatent allocates tokens dynamically according to visible part size. RoPE-anchored tokens preserve observed surface evidence, while no-RoPE completion tokens represent unobserved regions. A geometry latent enters through cross-attention, and alternating part-local and global attention layers complete all parts into a consistent full-object part layout.

Figure 5.Surface part segmentation and amodal completion results.For each example, OmniLatent produces complete surface part segmentation and further completes partial surface masks into complete object-level parts, preserving global structure while recovering missing components.

Figure 6.Qualitative comparison of surface part segmentationon PartObjaverse-Tiny-wt. OmniLatent produces semantically coherent regions and cleaner boundaries by decoding part IDs from a latent space aligned with geometry and appearance.

Figure 7.Point-prompted part control.OmniLatent supports three prompt-driven editing modes: (a) Full segmentation from sparse point prompts, (b) Part refine for correcting an initialized segmentation, and (c) Part subdivision for splitting a coarse part into finer components.

Figure 8.Qualitative comparison on amodal part completion.Given full geometry and partial surface masks, OmniLatent preserves visible part evidence and completes coherent full-object parts, producing cleaner part geometry and more consistent object structure than X-Part, HoloPart, PartPacker, and OmniPart.

Figure 9.Visual comparison of geometry generation. Despite its unified design, our method still produces high-quality generations, providing strong geometric understanding that benefits part decomposition.

Figure 10.Unified generation and mask-guided surface part segmentation.OmniLatent jointly generates geometry, deformation, appearance, and surface part IDs from a single image, and can use 2D segmentation masks as controllable guidance for part granularity.
Figure 11.Ablation study on Part ID representation and pretraining.
Figure 12.Ablation study on Condition-Aware 3D Rotary Position Embedding.
Figure 13.Limitations.OmniLatent can still produce asymmetric part layouts on symmetric structures and may mistakenly merge semantically distinct regions into a single part.
